headline_marked: [[PM Tarique Rahman returns to Dhaka]] after five-day US visit for UN General Assembly
headline: PM Tarique Rahman returns to Dhaka after five-day US visit for UN General Assembly
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman concluded his five-day visit to the United States, where he attended the 81st session of the UN General Assembly and delivered his maiden address. He arrived back in Dhaka this morning.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman returned to Dhaka this morning, concluding his five-day visit to the United States. He attended the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) during his trip.

An Emirates flight, carrying the Prime Minister, his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman, and entourage, landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport via Dubai around 8:21 AM. This was confirmed by PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.
The journey included a six-hour transit stop in Dubai. The flight departed Dubai International Airport for Dhaka at 2:15 AM local time after Tarique Rahman arrived from New York on Saturday evening.

In New York, Tarique Rahman and Dr Zubaida Rahman were seen off by Bangladesh Ambassador to the US Tareq Md Ariful Islam, Bangladesh’s Permanent Representative to the UN Irene Khan, and other senior officials.
The Prime Minister had arrived in New York on September 21 to participate in the UNGA. He delivered his maiden address as prime minister at the general debate on September 24.

During his busy five-day visit, Prime Minister Rahman held approximately 30 bilateral and side meetings. These engagements were with various heads of state and government, senior international officials, and representatives of international organisations.
caption:

headline_marked: [[Salman Muqtadir's studio attacked]] over 'extortion refusal'; 2 held in Dhaka
headline: Salman Muqtadir's studio attacked over 'extortion refusal'; 2 held in Dhaka
summary: Content creator Salman Muqtadir's studio in Dhaka was vandalized and looted on Saturday night following his alleged refusal to pay extortion money. The incident has sparked strong condemnation from the AB Party.
details: Content creator Salman Muqtadir's studio at New Greeny Properties in ECB Square, Dhaka, was attacked and vandalized on Saturday night. Muqtadir alleged the incident occurred after he refused to pay extortion money. He shared a video of the destruction on his verified Facebook page.

The Amar Bangladesh Party (AB Party) has expressed strong anger and concern over the incident, stating it should not be taken lightly. They highlighted Muqtadir as a known figure from the July mass uprising, adding gravity to the attack.

In a joint statement, AB Party's Senior Vice Chairman Wahab Minar and General Secretary Asaduzzaman Fuad questioned the state of law and order. They asked who ordinary citizens can turn to for security if armed miscreants dare to carry out such acts openly in the capital.

The party leaders emphasized that the July mass aspirations included an end to fear, occupation, extortion, and political terrorism. They warned that a return of such dominance and terror, even under new guises, would be a betrayal of the people's trust.

AB Party called for the swift arrest of the accused, urging authorities to take the allegations seriously. They stressed that criminals should not be allowed to escape justice based on political identity.
